name: Algeria
headline: Algeria is rolling out a national electronic record tied to the national ID, but patients get no sharing choices and no portal yet.

access.summary: Law 18-07 gives a right to a copy of one's data, requested provider by provider, and the controller may ask the regulator for longer reply times. The ministry's citizen app to view the record and test results is announced, not live.
detail: Article 34 of Law 18-07 lets a person obtain confirmation of processing and a copy of their data in intelligible form, with any information on its source.

No fixed reply deadline is set for access: the controller can ask the national authority for response times. Whether access is free was not verified; only rectification is stated to be free, within 10 days.
The 2018 health law gives every person a right to be informed about their health and care, but no explicit right to a copy of the chart was found in it.
In July 2026 the ministry said it is building an official app to show citizens their electronic record and test results. The CNAS El Hanaa app covers insurance tasks, not clinical records.

control.summary: The new national electronic record links each patient by national ID and lets authorised professionals anywhere in the country see it. No patient opt-out, consent setting or patient-visible access log was found.
detail: Law 18-11 requires every patient to have a single national medical record, and requires public and private facilities to keep a computerised one and join the national health information system.
The right to object in Article 36 of Law 18-07 does not apply when processing meets a legal obligation, which covers the mandated record.

Law 25-11 requires controllers to keep an automated log of processing operations, but its use is limited to legality checks, internal control, security and criminal procedure. It is not a patient-facing access log.
Reports on the rollout describe access by professionals "with the required authorisations", with no patient controls described.

privacy.summary: Health data is sensitive data under Law 18-07, refusing access rights can bring up to two years in prison, and an independent authority sits under the Presidency. With no health-sector enforcement or general breach-notice duty verified, it sits at the floor of the general-law band.
detail: Article 18 bans processing sensitive data, including health and genetic data, except with express consent, a legal basis, vital interest or the authority's permission.

The ANPDP was created under the President of the Republic with financial and administrative autonomy. It can warn, suspend and fine, and its rules on video surveillance (March 2026) show it is active.
Law 25-11 adds a mandatory data protection officer and records of processing. Its 5-day breach notice sits in the new law-enforcement title; a general breach duty was not verified.
Transfers abroad need the authority's approval. Algeria has no EU adequacy decision, and the EU's EHDS does not apply.

commercial.summary: Automated marketing by email, phone or fax needs prior consent, people may object to commercial prospecting, and sensitive data cannot be processed without a legal ground. No rules on health data brokers or sale of de-identified data were found.
detail: Article 37 of Law 18-07 bans direct marketing by automated means without prior consent, with a narrow exception for existing customers who get a free way to refuse.
Article 36 gives a right to object to use of one's data for prospecting, notably commercial.
Sending data abroad without authorisation carries one to five years in prison and fines up to DZD 1,000,000.
In July 2026 a ministry official warned citizens against unofficial health apps that ask for their health data. No specific rule for such apps was found.

journey.summary: Insurance claims are linked through the CNAS Chifa smart card used by doctors, pharmacists and labs. The national electronic record started rolling out in July 2026 in 10 pilot wilayas, with a 15 November 2026 deadline for all facilities.
detail: The Chifa card carries entitlements, emergency and chronic illness data, and lets providers create and send signed electronic claims to CNAS. Pharmacies use it for third-party payment.
The ministry launched the national rollout on 25 July 2026, selecting over 200 trainers in 10 pilot wilayas, aiming at 69 wilayas and over 2,500 facilities.
The health minister set 15 November 2026 as a deadline for all facilities to activate the system, with weekly progress reports.
A framework agreement will connect 2,599 health facilities by fibre. Electronic prescribing was not verified.

clinical.summary: The new record is designed so authorised clinicians anywhere can look up a patient by national ID or ID card. Until rollout finishes, past the 15 November 2026 deadline, most clinicians still work from separate facility records.
detail: Law 18-11 requires a single national medical record per patient, with details left to regulation.
The record is to hold medical history, examinations, treatments and blood group, according to the rollout report.
The first phase digitised emergency departments, with patient check-in, queues and triage.
Actual share of facilities live on the system was not verified.

research.summary: Health research using personal data needs ANPDP authorisation and clinical studies need written, withdrawable consent. There is no general opt-out from secondary use, and no public register of uses was found.
detail: Article 21 of Law 18-07 makes processing for public-interest health research subject to authorisation by the national authority.
Law 18-11 requires free, express, informed written consent for clinical studies, limited to that study and revocable at any time, plus ministry authorisation.
Facilities must send data for epidemiological surveys and health statistics, without consent.
Score: base 40, plus 3 for the permit body and 3 for criminal penalties for misuse.

ai.summary: Under the 2018 health law, software built into a medical device is covered and devices need ANPP approval, but no rules for standalone or AI software on validation, change control or oversight were found. A national AI strategy is only now being put into practice.
detail: Article 212 of Law 18-11 includes accessories and software involved in a device's functioning in the definition of a medical device; Article 230 requires approval by the national pharmaceutical products agency before marketing.
The ANPP list of device texts holds 2021 orders on approval files and changes, none on AI.
An interministerial commission to carry out the AI strategy was installed on 5 August 2026.
The ministry plans AI-assisted remote imaging; rules for it were not found.
